why:
2026-09-28 — an UPSTREAM name on an ours-only type, which is why it needs a row of its own rather than inheriting `cpp:ClientHandle`'s, the same reason `cpp:ClientHandle::async_send_request` has one. The substantive verdict against `rclcpp::ClientBase::service_is_ready` — the name, and the `ResultOf<bool>` shape RFC-0018 forces — stays at `cpp:Client::service_is_ready`; this row records that the verb is ALSO on the handle, and why it can be.

WHY IT CAN BE, and it is the same sentence `async_send_request`'s row writes: it needs `{executor, handle_id}` and nothing else. `nros_cpp_service_client_server_available` read an `RmwServiceClient` in CALLER storage until 2026-09-28 and now takes `(storage, executor, handle_id)` — the shape issue 1437 gave the granted-QoS accessor — so the two words this handle already carries are the whole probe road. No member was added to the handle.

WHY IT MATTERS ON THIS TYPE PARTICULARLY: `Client<S>::SharedPtr` is what a ported member declaration produces, so this is the object a ported node actually holds when it asks whether its server is up. Between phase-456 W9 and this closure it could not ask at all, which is the gap written up at `cpp:Client::wait_for_service`. Held by `ros2_api_adoption_stage2.cpp`, which calls both verbs on a `Client<S>::SharedPtr` member in the ported hosted shape, and by `rclcpp_node_freestanding_surface.cpp`, which instantiates them with no STL at all. Also held by the two-directional reachability assertions in `tests/compile/ros2_api_adoption.cpp` — this pair IS reachable on both the dispatch client and the handle, `send_request` still is NOT, and the handle is still two words — the shape `cpp:ClientHandle::async_send_request` uses, because a silent loss of a method would leave every other assertion about this type green.
